αὐτοῦ, αἰτία προφητείας καὶ ἀνακαινισμοῦ καὶ οὐρανίων ἀγαθῶν καὶ τοῦ κατανοεῖν τὸ κάλλος τῆς θεϊκῆς ἀληθείας ἐστίν. ὡς γὰρ τῷ ἀποστόλῳ δοκεῖ· «ὁ καρπὸς τοῦ πνεύματος ἀγάπη, χαρά, εἰρήνη ἐστίν.» ὅθεν καὶ πάλιν γράφει· «ἡ γὰρ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκκέχυται ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν ἐν πνεύ ματι ἁγίῳ.» μιᾶς γοῦν οὔσης ἀγαθότητος τῆς ἐν ἑνάδι τριάδος, πολλαὶ ἡμῖν ἀποτίκτονται ἀγαθότητος· ὥσπερ ἀληθείας καὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ σοφίας μιᾶς οὔσης τῆς ἄνω φημί κατὰ τό· «δυνατὸς εἶ, κύριε, καὶ ἡ ἀλήθειά σου κύκλῳ σου,» ἥτις ἐστὶν ὁ μονογενὴς θεός καὶ κατὰ τό· «μόνῳ σοφῷ θεῷ» πολλαὶ πληθύνονται ἡμῖν ἄνωθεν ἀλήθειαι καὶ δικαιοσύναι καὶ σοφίαι κατὰ τό· «ἀληθείας ἐκζητεῖ κύριος,» καί· «δίκαιος κύριος καὶ δικαιοσύνας ἠγάπησεν», καί· «πλῆθος σοφῶν, σωτηρία κόσμου», καί· «συμπορευόμενος σοφοῖς, σοφὸς ἔσῃ.» σαφὲς οὖν, ὡς πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ ὑπάρξει αὐτῇ πνεῦμα ἀγαθὸν καὶ πνεῦμα σοφίας καὶ ἀληθείας καὶ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἀοράτου καὶ ἀσυνθέτου θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς καθέστηκεν. 6.9ν ὅτι φιλάνθρωπον ἡ κτίσις οὐ γέγραπται φιλάνθρωπος· ἴδιον γὰρ τοῦτο κυρίως μόνης τῆς ὁμοουσίου τριάδος. φιλάνθρωπος γὰρ ὁ πατήρ· «οὐχ ἕως τέλους ἡμῖν ὀργιζόμενος, οὐδ' εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα μηνιῶν, οὐδὲ ποιῶν ἡμῖν πρὸς τὰς ἁμαρτίας, οὐδὲ κατὰ τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν ἀνταποδιδούς,» κατὰ τὸν ρβʹ ψαλμόν· καὶ ὡς Σολομὼν λέγει· «φείδῃ δὲ πάντων, ὅτι πάντα σά ἐστιν, δέσποτα φιλόψυχε,» καθὰ εἴρηται· ὡς καὶ διὰ ταῦτα καλεῖσθαι ἡμῶν δεσπότην τε καὶ πατέρα, τῆς κηδεμονίας αὐτοῦ τῇ δυνάμει κεκραμένης. τῷ θεῷ γὰρ οὐκ ἔστιν πρόσρησις οἰκειοτέρα τῆς πατρὸς καὶ φιλανθρώπου καὶ ἀγαθοῦ καὶ ἁγίου. φιλάνθρωπος ὁ υἱὸς, ὅς γε δι' ἡμᾶς, τὰ ἔργα τῶν σεπτῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ νοητῶν χειρῶν· «ἑαυτὸν ἐκένωσεν, μορφὴν δούλου λαβών·» καθὰ Τίτῳ γράφει ὁ ἀπόστολος· «ὅτε δὲ ἡ χρηστότης καὶ ἡ φιλανθρωπία τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν θεοῦ ἐπ εφάνη.» καὶ ὅστις ἂν ἀπονείμῃ αὐτῷ, ὅσα πρέπει μονογενεῖ θεῷ, λαβὼν πλέον ὧν ἤλπισεν, ἀπέρχεται. φιλάνθρωπον τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ κατὰ τὴν Σοφίαν, οὕτω λέγουσαν· «φιλάνθρωπον γὰρ πνεῦμα σοφίας, καὶ οὐκ ἀθωώσει δίκαιον.» οὐ γὰρ παρεῖδεν ἀπολλυμένην τὴν ἀνθρωπείαν φύσιν· ἀλλ' ἐφοίτησεν δι' ἑαυτοῦ ὁδηγῆσαν, διδάξαν πᾶσαν ἀλήθειαν, ἀνακαινίσαν ἡμᾶς, καὶ τὰ θεϊκὰ χαρίσματα δωρησάμενον, καὶ τοσαύτην τοῦ κατ' εἰκόνα θέμενον ἀνέκαθεν φροντίδα, ὥστε εἰς γνώρισμα τῆς ὑπερφυοῦς αὐτοῦ ἀγαθότητος καὶ ταύτην ἔχειν τὴν προσηγορίαν. μεγάλα μὲν γὰρ στοιχεῖα οὐρανός, γῆ, θάλασσα· μεγάλη δὲ λογικὴ κτίσις, ἡ ἀγγέλων καὶ πάσης ὑπερκοσμίου δυνάμεως· ἀλλ' οὐκ ἀφ' ἑνὸς τούτων ἠξίωσεν, ἐκ δὲ τῆς πρὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἀγαθότητος ἔχει ὄνομα τὸ φιλάνθρωπον ἡ τριάς. 6.10ν ὅτι φύσει ἐλεύθερον καὶ οὐ δοῦλον· καὶ ὡς θεὸς καὶ κύριος ἐλευθεροῖ καὶ υἱοὺς ποιεῖ. ἡ κτίσις δούλη τοῦ τεχνησαμένου αὐτὴν δεσπότου καθέστηκεν, ἐλευθερίαν, ἣ ἀφ' ἑαυτῆς μὴ κέκτηται, οὔτε ἑαυτῇ οὔτ' ἄλλοις παρέχειν δυναμένη. φησὶν γὰρ ἡ προφητεία· «τὰ σύμπαντα δοῦλά σα.» τὸ δὲ ἅγιον πνεῦμα μονονουχὶ δοῦλον οὐ γέγραπται, ἀλλὰ καὶ 62 ὡς δεσπότης καὶ φύσει ἐλεύθερον, ἔνθα ἐστὶν καὶ οἷς ἐπιφοιτᾷ, ἐλευθερίαν, ἣν ἔχει, παρέχει. τὰ γὰρ ποιήματα μόνα τῷ τῆς δουλείας ὑπάγεται ζυγῷ· τὸ δὲ μὴ δοῦλον, οὐδὲ ποίημα· τὸ δὲ μὴ ποίημα, φύσει θεός· μάρτυς δὲ τούτων πιστὸς ὁ ἀπόστολος, γράφων Κορινθίοις μὲν ἐν τῇ δευτέρα ἐπιστολῇ· «ὁ δὲ κύριος τὸ πνεῦμά ἐστιν· οὗ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα κυρίου, ἐκεῖ ἐλευ θερία,» Τιμοθέῳ δέ· «οὐ γὰρ ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ θεὸς πνεῦμα δουλείας, ἀλλὰ πνεῦμα δυνάμεως καὶ ἀγάπης καὶ σωφρονισμοῦ,» Ῥωμαίοις δέ· «οὐ γὰρ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα δουλείας πάλιν εἰς φόβον, ἀλλὰ πνεῦμα υἱο θεσίας, ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν· ἀββά, ὁ πατήρ,» Γαλάταις δέ· «ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν κράζον· ἀββά, ὁ πατήρ. ὥστε οὐκέτι εἶ δοῦλος, ἀλλ' υἱός.» καθάπερ οὖν ἠλευθερώθημεν παρὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ ἀκούσαντες· «οὐκέτι εἶ δοῦλος, ἀλλ' ἐλεύθερος,» καί· «τῇ ἐλευθερίᾳ, ᾗ ὁ υἱὸς ὑμᾶς ἠλευθέρωσεν·» οὕτω διὰ τὸ ταὐτὸν τῆς οὐσίας καὶ δεσποτείας ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος ἠλευθερούμεθα διὰ τοῦ μνημονευθέντος ῥήματος· «οὗ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα κυρίου, ἐκεῖ ἐλευθερία.» 6.11ν ὅτι ἐπιτάσσει, οὐχ ὑπουργεῖ ἡ κτίσις, ἤ τε νοερὰ καὶ αἰσθητή, ὑπουργεῖ, οὐκ ἐπιτάττει ἀφ' ἑαυτῆς· ὡς περὶ τῶν ἀγγέλων pass_a_gloss: [Continuing the quotation from the previous section: 'And God who knows the heart bore witness to them, giving the Holy Spirit, just as also to us;] and he made no distinction between us and them, having cleansed their hearts by faith.' That is: the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, or, as one might say, his unrestrained and unstinting coming upon us, is the cause of prophecy and of renewal and of heavenly goods and of perceiving the beauty of the divine truth. For as the apostle holds: 'The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace.' Hence he also writes again: 'For the love of God has been poured out in our hearts in the Holy Spirit.' So, though the goodness of the Trinity in unity is one, many goodnesses are born for us; just as, though truth and righteousness and wisdom are one, I mean the one above, according to: 'You are mighty, Lord, and your truth is round about you,' which truth is the only-begotten God, and according to: 'to the only wise God,' many truths and righteousnesses and wisdoms are multiplied for us from above, according to: 'The Lord seeks out truths,' and: 'The Lord is righteous and loved righteousnesses,' and: 'A multitude of wise men is the salvation of the world,' and: 'Walking with the wise, you will be wise.' It is clear then that the Spirit of God, in his very existence, is established as a good Spirit, and a Spirit of wisdom and of truth, and the Spirit of the invisible and uncompounded God and Father. 6.9ν [Chapter title:] That it loves mankind. The creation is not written to be a lover of mankind; for this is properly peculiar to the consubstantial Trinity alone. For the Father loves mankind: 'not being angry with us to the end, nor wrathful for ever, nor dealing with us according to our sins, nor repaying according to our iniquities,' according to the hundred and second Psalm; and as Solomon says: 'But you spare all things, because all things are yours, Master, lover of souls,' as has been said; so that for these reasons too he is called our Master and Father, his care being blended with his power. For there is no title more proper to God than that of Father and lover of mankind and good and holy. The Son loves mankind, he who for our sake, the works of his revered and spiritual hands, 'emptied himself, taking the form of a servant,' as the apostle writes to Titus: 'But when the kindness and the love for mankind of God our Saviour appeared.' And whoever assigns to him all that befits the only-begotten God goes away having received more than he hoped. The Holy Spirit of God loves mankind, according to Wisdom, which says thus: 'For the spirit of wisdom loves mankind, and will not acquit the righteous.' For he did not overlook human nature perishing; but he came by himself, guiding, teaching all truth, renewing us, and bestowing the divine gifts, and from the first taking such care of what was made after the image that, as a token of his surpassing goodness, he has this title too. For great elements are heaven, earth, sea; and great is the rational creation, that of angels and of every power above the world; but not from any one of these did it see fit to be named; rather, from its goodness toward man the Trinity has the name 'lover of mankind'. 6.10ν [Chapter title:] That it is free by nature and not a slave; and as God and Lord it sets free and makes sons. The creation stands as slave of the Master who crafted it, unable to provide freedom, which it does not possess from itself, either to itself or to others. For the prophecy says: 'All things are your slaves.' But the Holy Spirit not only is not written as a slave, but is written also [printed line number 62, page debris] as master and free by nature, and where he is and to those whom he visits he provides the freedom which he has. For things made alone are brought under the yoke of slavery; what is not a slave is not a thing made either; and what is not a thing made is God by nature. And a faithful witness of these things is the apostle, writing to the Corinthians in the second epistle: 'Now the Lord is the Spirit; and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom'; and to Timothy: 'For God did not give us a spirit of slavery, but a spirit of power and of love and of self-control'; and to the Romans: 'For you did not receive a spirit of slavery again to fear, but a spirit of adoption, in which we cry: Abba, Father'; and to the Galatians: 'God sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying: Abba, Father. So you are no longer a slave, but a son.' Just as, then, we were set free by the Son, having heard: 'You are no longer a slave, but free,' and: 'in the freedom with which the Son set you free,' so, because of the sameness of the substance and of the lordship, we are set free by the Spirit, through the saying already mentioned: 'Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.' 6.11ν [Chapter title:] That it commands and does not serve. The creation, both the intellectual and the perceptible, serves; it does not command from itself; as it says about the angels: 'mighty in strength, doing the word [the quotation continues in the next section].
pass_b_english: “…and he made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith” (Acts 15:9). That is, the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, or, as one might put it, his unrestrained and unstinting coming upon us, is the cause of prophecy and renewal, of heavenly goods, and of seeing the beauty of divine truth. For, as the apostle holds, “the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace” (Galatians 5:22). That is why he writes again, “For the love of God has been poured out in our hearts by the Holy Spirit” (Romans 5:5).

So, though the goodness of the Trinity in unity is one, many forms of goodness are born for us. In the same way, truth and righteousness and wisdom above are one. I mean the truth of which Scripture says, “You are mighty, Lord, and your truth is round about you” (Psalm 89:8), and that truth is the only-begotten God; and the wisdom of which it says, “to the only wise God” (Romans 16:27). Yet many truths and righteousnesses and wisdoms are multiplied for us from above, as it is written: “The Lord seeks out truths” (Psalm 30:24 LXX), and, “The Lord is righteous and has loved righteous deeds” (Psalm 11:7), and, “A multitude of the wise is the salvation of the world” (Wisdom of Solomon 6:24), and, “Walk with the wise and you will be wise” (Proverbs 13:20). It is clear, then, that the Spirit of God is, in his very existence, a good Spirit, a Spirit of wisdom and truth, the Spirit of the invisible and uncompounded God and Father.

Creation is nowhere written to be a lover of mankind, for that belongs properly to the consubstantial Trinity alone. The Father loves mankind: “He is not angry with us to the end, nor wrathful for ever; he does not deal with us according to our sins, nor repay us according to our iniquities,” as the hundred and third Psalm says (Psalm 103:9-10). And as Solomon says, “But you spare all things, because all things are yours, O Master, lover of souls” (Wisdom of Solomon 11:26), as has been said. For these reasons too he is called our Master and our Father, since his care is blended with his power. No title is more proper to God than Father, lover of mankind, good and holy.

The Son loves mankind. For our sake, who are the works of his holy hands, hands to be understood spiritually, “he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant” (Philippians 2:7). So the apostle writes to Titus: “But when the kindness and the love for mankind of God our Saviour appeared” (Titus 3:4). Whoever gives him all that befits the only-begotten God goes away having received more than he hoped for.

The Holy Spirit of God loves mankind, as Wisdom says: “For the spirit of wisdom loves mankind, and will not acquit the righteous” (Wisdom of Solomon 1:6). He did not overlook human nature as it perished. He came of his own accord, guiding us, teaching all truth, renewing us, and bestowing the divine gifts. From the beginning he took such care of the creature made after the image that he bears this title too, as a token of his surpassing goodness. Heaven, earth and sea are great elements. Great too is the rational creation of angels and of every power above the world. But the Trinity did not choose to be named from any of these. From its goodness toward man it has the name “lover of mankind.”
That he is free by nature and not a slave; and that, as God and Lord, he sets free and makes sons.

Creation is the slave of the Master who crafted it. It does not possess freedom of itself, and it cannot give freedom either to itself or to others. For the prophecy says, “All things are your slaves” (Psalm 119:91). But the Holy Spirit is not only never written as a slave; he is also written as Master and free by nature. Wherever he is, and to those he visits, he gives the freedom he has. Only things made are brought under the yoke of slavery. What is not a slave is not a thing made, and what is not a thing made is God by nature.

The apostle is a faithful witness of this. He writes to the Corinthians in the second epistle, “Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom” (2 Corinthians 3:17); to Timothy, “For God did not give us a spirit of slavery, but a spirit of power and of love and of self-control” (2 Timothy 1:7); to the Romans, “For you did not receive a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but a spirit of adoption, in whom we cry, ‘Abba, Father’” (Romans 8:15); and to the Galatians, “God sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, ‘Abba, Father.’ So you are no longer a slave, but a son” (Galatians 4:6-7). Just as we were set free by the Son when we heard, “You are no longer a slave, but free,” and, “in the freedom with which the Son set you free” (Galatians 5:1), so too, because the substance and the lordship are the same, we are set free by the Spirit, through the saying already quoted: “Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom” (2 Corinthians 3:17).
That he commands and does not serve.
Creation, whether spiritual or perceived by the senses, serves; it does not command of itself. As is said of the angels, “mighty in strength, doing the word…” (Psalm 103:20).

choices.issue: Garbled machine draft, wrong Psalm number, chapter titles run into the text, abbreviated references
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u15): retranslated from the Greek. The reader report (titus/SOURCE_ISSUES.md) flagged 'according to Psalm 24 (Psalm 103:9-10)': the Greek is ρβʹ, the hundred and second Psalm, English Psalm 103; now 'the hundred and third Psalm (Psalm 103:9-10)'. The Titus reference itself (Titus 3:4) was right and is kept. The old English also read σεπτῶν as 'seven' ('his seven and intelligible hands'), ἀσυνθέτου as 'indivisible', made the Wisdom 1:6 quotation into '[he is] a man of a spirit of wisdom', broke the chapter title 6.9 across two paragraphs ('phil...'), ran the titles 6.10 and 6.11 into the text as '[he is] free' and 'he commands, and creation does not serve', and said the Spirit is not written 'a slave alone'. References: (2 Cor 3:17), (2 Tim 1:7), (Rom 8:15), (Gal 4:6) written out, Galatians 4:6 -> 4:6-7; Acts 15:9, Psalm 89:8, Romans 16:27, Psalm 30:24 LXX, Psalm 11:7, Wisdom 6:24, Proverbs 13:20, Wisdom 11:26, Wisdom 1:6, Galatians 5:1, the second 2 Corinthians 3:17 and Psalm 103:20 added. Bracket fillers [that of], [he is], [us], [of God] removed.

choices.why: The section opens inside the quotation of Acts 15:8-9 begun in the previous section; only these words are translated, with an opening ellipsis inside the quotation.
Each chapter title becomes its own paragraph without the number.

choices.english: many forms of goodness are born for us
choices.why: ἀγαθότητος is read as the plural ἀγαθότητες (the copy-text's ending looks like a slip); the plural matches 'many truths and righteousnesses and wisdoms' below.
Didymus' point rests on the plurals of LXX Psalm 30:24 and 10:7; 'righteous deeds' keeps the plural of δικαιοσύνας in natural English.
The Greek Psalm reads 'truths' where the Hebrew and KJV (Psalm 31:23) read 'the faithful'; cited in Greek numbering with LXX, as the reference gate requires.

choices.english: as the hundred and third Psalm says (Psalm 103:9-10)

choices.term: τὰ ἔργα τῶν σεπτῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ νοητῶν χειρῶν
choices.english: who are the works of his holy hands, hands to be understood spiritually
choices.why: The phrase stands in apposition to ἡμᾶς; νοητῶν marks the 'hands' as spoken of God, not bodily.

choices.term: καὶ οὐκ ἀθωώσει δίκαιον (Wisdom of Solomon 1:6)
choices.english: and will not acquit the righteous
choices.why: Translated as the copy-text reads. The Greek Bible has ‘will not acquit a blasphemer from his lips’ (οὐκ ἀθῳώσει βλάσφημον); δίκαιον may be a corruption. Recorded in problems.

choices.english: He came of his own accord
choices.why: δι' ἑαυτοῦ: by himself, on his own initiative, not sent as a servant.

choices.english: the creature made after the image
choices.why: The standard patristic phrase for man made in God's image (Genesis 1:26-27); 'creature made' is added so the phrase reads in English.

choices.term: ἀλλ' οὐκ ἀφ' ἑνὸς τούτων ἠξίωσεν
choices.english: But the Trinity did not choose to be named from any of these
choices.why: The subject, ἡ τριάς, is given at the end of the Greek sentence and moved forward; 'to be named' completes ἠξίωσεν from the following ἔχει ὄνομα.

choices.term: μονονουχὶ δοῦλον οὐ γέγραπται, ἀλλὰ καὶ
choices.english: is not only never written as a slave; he is also written as Master
choices.why: Didymus uses μονονουχί with οὐ ... ἀλλὰ καί for 'not only not ... but also'.

choices.english: he is also written as Master
choices.why: 62 is a printed line number, page debris; skipped.
Didymus' text has δουλείας ('slavery') where the New Testament has δειλίας ('cowardice'); his reading is translated because his argument depends on it.

choices.english: “You are no longer a slave, but free”
choices.why: A memory blend of Galatians 4:7 and 4:31 with 'free' for 'son'; no inline reference (listed as a possible allusion). The next words, 'the freedom with which the Son set you free', are Galatians 5:1 with 'the Son' for 'Christ'.

choices.term: τὸ ταὐτὸν τῆς οὐσίας καὶ δεσποτείας
choices.english: because the substance and the lordship are the same
choices.why: The Spirit sets free as the Son does because he shares the Son's substance and lordship.
The quotation of Psalm 103:20 (Greek 102:20) runs on into the next section, which holds its last word αὐτοῦ ('his'); the English ends with an ellipsis and does not supply it here.
